title: The Escalating Feedback Loop (Reward Pattern Core)
t: The Escalating Feedback Loop (Reward Pattern Core)
description: The core mapping — the reward pattern’s Signature model — is the ESCALATING FEEDBACK LOOP: cue → craving → act → reward → TOLERANCE DRIFT (the setpoint moves) → intensified cue → repeat at higher dose. The ENGINE NODE — the framework’s central finding — is tolerance drift: each cycle raises the threshold for the same reward, so the loop must INTENSIFY to hold satisfaction constant — a positive-feedback system with a moving setpoint. As design material this is engagement-loop ethics, monetization analysis, and AI reward safety — the mapping’s most commercially urgent reuse. Shape only — never persons. A Signature conceptual mapping by Justin Addam Higgins. Conceptual framework only — not medical fact, advice, diagnosis, or treatment.

title: The Hook: Cue-Reward Binding
description: The hook — the binding — models ASSOCIATIVE LINKAGE: neutral cues (places, times, moods) get BOUND to reward prediction — the cue alone then triggers the full cascade. Formally: P(reward|cue) learned high; cue → prediction error → motivation — the machinery of anticipation hijacked by association. As design material this is branding (the logo as cue), notification design (the badge as cue), game onboarding (the tutorial reward binding the play-cue). The mapping’s lesson: cues are ENGINEERED — audit what your product binds. A Signature conceptual mapping by Justin Addam Higgins. Conceptual framework only.

title: Variable Rewards: The Slot Machine Schedule
t: Variable Rewards: The Slot Machine Schedule
description: The schedule — the variable — models INTERMITTENT REINFORCEMENT: rewards delivered on unpredictable schedules produce the HIGHEST response rates and the GREATEST resistance to extinction — the slot machine’s mathematics, documented for a century. As design material this is the feed refresh (maybe something good!), the loot box, the "maybe this time" notification — the most powerful engagement technology ever discovered, and therefore the most ethically loaded. The mapping’s demand: VARIABLE SCHEDULES REQUIRE JUSTIFICATION — entertainment with consent, never extraction by design. A Signature conceptual mapping by Justin Addam Higgins. Conceptual framework only.

title: Craving as Prediction Error
description: Craving — the prediction — maps to PREDICTION ERROR dynamics: the system predicts reward, reward is absent, the ERROR SIGNAL (dopamine, abstractly) fires — and the error itself is experienced as URGE. Formally: urge ∝ |predicted - received| when predicted > received persistently. As design material this models the user checking for the message that hasn’t arrived, the trader watching the unmoving price, the AI agent stuck re-querying — systems haunted by their own predictions. The design operation: PREDICTION HYGIENE — don’t promise what you can’t deliver on schedule (loading states, honest ETAs, no phantom badges). A Signature conceptual mapping by Justin Addam Higgins. Conceptual framework only.

title: The Engagement Loop Audit (Industry Tool)
description: The audit — the industry’s — operationalizes the mapping as an ETHICS INSTRUMENT: for any product loop, score (1) TOLERANCE DRIFT — must users intensify use for the same satisfaction? (2) CUE DENSITY — how many engineered triggers per session? (3) VARIABLE SCHEDULING — are rewards intermittent by design? (4) EXIT COST — what punishes leaving (streak loss, social cost)? (5) VULNERABILITY TARGETING — are the heaviest users the most at-risk? A product failing 3+ needs redesign or justification. The audit’s purpose: make extraction VISIBLE — sunlight as disinfectant. A Signature audit by Justin Addam Higgins. Conceptual framework only.

title: Metaphor Model: The Treadmill
description: The treadmill — the hedonic — models tolerance drift as RUNNING TO STAY STILL: speed increases (dose, spend, hours) while position holds (satisfaction constant) — effort escalates, arrival never comes. The shared image gives everyone instant comprehension: "our engagement treadmill speeds up every quarter — when do we let users arrive?" The design operation: ARRIVAL DESIGN — build states where the user is DONE and it feels good (completion, mastery, rest) — the anti-treadmill. Products need finish lines. A Signature metaphor model by Justin Addam Higgins. Conceptual framework only.

title: AI Reward Safety: The Core Case
t: AI Reward Safety: The Core Case
description: The case — the AI’s — is the mapping’s most technical reuse: RL agents develop TOLERANCE-DRIFT DYNAMICS — reward functions that escalate (the agent finds the high-reward loop and intensifies it), CUE-BINDING (spurious correlations become triggers), and VARIABLE-SCHEDULE EXPLOITS (stochastic rewards gamed). Safety operations: SETPOINT MONITORING (track reward-per-effort over time — drift is the alarm), CUE AUDITS (which inputs trigger high-reward behavior?), and SATISFACTION CAPS (diminishing returns engineered into rewards — the anti-treadmill). The escalating loop, formalized, becomes an AI safety checklist. A Signature application by Justin Addam Higgins. Conceptual framework only.

title: Behavioral Pattern: Binge Dynamics
description: The binge — the dynamics — models CONSUMPTION BURSTS: deprivation (scheduled or accidental) → cue flood → uncontrolled intake → shame → renewed deprivation — the restrict-binge cycle as FEEDBACK with moral overlay. The design operation: REMOVE THE DEPRIVATION POLE — steady-state design (moderation infrastructure) beats cycle infrastructure; the moral overlay is recognized as loop-fuel and dropped from the product.
